radiology_report:
Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis | 05 Jan 2025 | Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical indication: Evaluation of elevated PSA (5.0 ng/mL) and prior PI-RADS 2 classification.

FINDINGS: Dimensions of the gland stand at 38 x 52 x 41 mm, yielding a calculated volume of 48.92 mL. T2 sequences reveal a uniform peripheral zone, free of focal signal anomalies. No restricted diffusion appears on DWI, while DCE sequences show neither early nor persistent enhancement. A 4 mm benign prostatic utricle cyst resides at the midline apex. Seminal vesicles exhibit normal caliber and signal characteristics. Extraprostatic extension and suspicious lymphadenopathy are absent.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 2. No PI-RADS 3+ lesion identified. PSA density: 0.1 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.8184269.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: A routine follow-up visit addressed a rising PSA trajectory that hit 4.5 ng/mL during February 2024. After reviewing the incremental risk, a urology referral was secured for multiparametric MRI to characterize the gland. COPD management continued as before, with instructions to flag any fresh urinary symptoms immediately.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: The annual assessment recorded a steady PSA at 3.4 ng/mL, mirroring the prior year’s results. Lower urinary tract symptoms persisted at a mild level (IPSS 5/35) and remained well-tolerated. Conservative monitoring proceeded, with a follow-up PSA check set for early 2024.
